Audition

aw-DISH-un · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A short performance where you show your skill and try to win a part in a show or on a team.

Dozens of dancers came to the audition for the spring show.

Worked Example

At her audition, Emma sang one song for the judges and hoped to win the lead role.

Emma performed a short piece for judges who would pick who gets the part. A 'show your skill and try to win a spot' performance is an audition.

How Audition Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

test

test: a check of what you know or can do

interview

interview: a meeting to try to win a job or a spot

Antonyms

invitation

invitation: being asked to join, with no test needed

guarantee

guarantee: a sure thing that needs no test

How Strong Is It? — practice → audition → premiere

practice vs. audition

practice vs. audition: A practice is less serious than an audition: practice is just training where nothing is decided, while an audition is a short test performance where judges decide if you win the part.

premiere vs. audition

premiere vs. audition: A premiere goes further than an audition: an audition is a short tryout to win a part, while a premiere is the first full show, with everything performed for a real audience.

The pieces

root — audi

suffix — tion

suffix — tion: an act or event

Put it together

Put it together: Audi means to hear. An audition began as a 'hearing' - the judges sit and hear you perform before they choose who gets the part.

Use the root in a new word: audience

Use the root in a new word: audience: The audience clapped and cheered when the play ended.

Word Choice

Audition can also be a verb: you audition for a play. Sports teams usually say tryout; theater and music say audition - same idea.
